body.statement:
For every support-cleaned coherent foldwise fit using \(\widehat R=\widehat D^{-1}\widehat B\widehat W\), the corrected \(\widehat N\), and the data-driven spectral inverse, if \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\), then, on an event whose probability tends to one,
\[
 \|E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\Delta_n,
\]
where
\[
 \Delta_n=r_m(r_\pi+r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}
 +(r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})R_{\Sigma}.
\]
In particular, the pathwise derivative of the mean bias is zero along a support-preserving two-sided perturbation of \(M_A\) alone and along a coherent perturbation of \(f\) alone.
body.justification: The cancellation proves that the finite efficiency correction remains orthogonal after data-driven support cleaning, with threshold cost entering only through cleaned measurement rates.
body.gap: Existing binary and categorical bridge results do not analyze this exact multilevel projector after threshold-and-renormalize support recovery.
body.consumer: It permits efficient inference under explicit products of cleaned exposure-measurement and outcome-regression errors.
body.proof_tex:
Work coordinatewise and put \(k=QU\) and \(\widehat k=\widehat Q\widehat U\).  The assumption \(r_{A,\infty}+r_{Z,\infty}=o_P(\tau_{S,n})\) is precisely \(\kappa_{\mathrm{supp},n}=o_P(1)\).  The support-cleaned conditional-zero lemma therefore applies on \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{clean},n}\), whose probability tends to one, and gives
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\left[
 (r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\right]. \tag{6}
\]
The established score-stability lemma, applied to the same cleaned coherent law and the corrected definition of \(R_\Sigma\), gives
\[
 \|\widehat k-k\|_{L^2(P)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}R_\Sigma. \tag{7}
\]
Combining (6) and (7),
\[
 \|E_P\widehat k\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{(r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})R_\Sigma
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\}. \tag{8}
\]

We next evaluate the raw bridge mean.  The fitted inverse bridges are formed from \(\bar M_A,\bar M_Z\).  For \(j,l\in\mathcal J\), define
\[
 \delta^A_{jl}(X)=E_P\{\widehat a_j(A,X)\mid J=l,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=l\},
 \qquad
 \delta^Z_{jl}(X)=E_P\{\widehat z_j(Z,X)\mid J=l,X\}-\mathbf 1\{j=l\}.
\]
By the bridge definitions and the true conditional measurement laws,
\[
 \delta^A=\bar M_A^{-1}M_A-I_K=\bar M_A^{-1}(M_A-\bar M_A),
 \qquad
 \delta^Z=\bar M_Z^{-1}M_Z-I_K=\bar M_Z^{-1}(M_Z-\bar M_Z). \tag{9}
\]
The cleaned singular-value half-margins and the support-cleaning algebra lemma imply
\[
 \|\delta^A\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^{\mathrm c},
 \qquad
 \|\delta^Z\|_{L^2(P_X)}\leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_Z^{\mathrm c}, \tag{10}
\]
and both matrices are uniformly bounded.

Conditional three-view independence separates \(Y,A,Z\) given \((J,X)\), and the definition of \(m_l\) gives \(E_P(Y-\widehat m_j\mid J=l,X)=m_l-\widehat m_j\).  Expanding \(\widehat U_j\), conditioning first on \((J,X)\), and summing over \(J\) yields the exact identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P(\widehat U_j\mid X)-m_j
={}&(\widehat m_j-m_j)
 \left[1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}
 (1+\delta^A_{jj})(1+\delta^Z_{jj})\right]\\
&+\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\sum_{l\ne j}\pi_l
 \delta^A_{jl}\delta^Z_{jl}(m_l-\widehat m_j).
\end{aligned} \tag{11}
\]
Indeed, when \(l=j\) the two conditional bridge means are \(1+\delta^A_{jj}\) and \(1+\delta^Z_{jj}\); when \(l\ne j\), both indicator terms vanish and only the product of the two errors remains.

Latent positivity and the fitted half-margin give \(\pi_j^{-1}\leq\varepsilon^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\pi_j^{-1}\leq2\varepsilon^{-1}\).  The true and fitted regressions are bounded by \(L\), because both laws use the declared bounded common outcome support.  Also
\[
 \left|1-\frac{\pi_j}{\widehat\pi_j}\right|
 \leq2\varepsilon^{-1}|\widehat\pi_j-\pi_j|.
\]
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz over \(P_X\) to the first line of (11), and use (10); its integrated absolute value is at most
\[
 C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_m(r_\pi+r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c}).
\]
Apply Cauchy--Schwarz to the product in the second line of (11), using fixed \(K\) and (10); its integrated absolute value is at most \(C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\).  Since \(E_Pm_j(X)=\psi_j\), the finite-dimensional norm satisfies
\[
 \|E_P\widehat U-\psi\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}\{r_m(r_\pi+r_A^{\mathrm c}+r_Z^{\mathrm c})
 +r_A^{\mathrm c}r_Z^{\mathrm c}\}. \tag{12}
\]
The mean of the fitted efficient score decomposes as
\[
 E_P(\widehat U-\widehat Q\widehat U)-\psi
 =(E_P\widehat U-\psi)-E_P\widehat k.
\]
Combining (8), (12), and the corrected definition of \(\Delta_n\) proves the displayed bias bound.

For the derivative assertions, let \(t\mapsto\eta_t\) be a support-preserving two-sided regular factor path through the truth and evaluate its score mean under \(P=P_{\eta_0}\).  If only \(M_A\) varies, then \(m_t=m\), \(\pi_t=\pi\), and \(\delta^Z_t=0\), so (11) gives \(E_PU(\eta_t)-\psi=0\) for all sufficiently small \(t\).  Support preservation makes the exact conditional-zero cancellation applicable, and the preceding argument with \(r_Z=0\) gives
\[
 \|E_PQ(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)\|
 \leq C_{\mathrm{reg}}r_A(t)
 \|Q(\eta_t)U(\eta_t)-QU\|_2=O(t^2),
\]
because DQM differentiability gives \(r_A(t)=O(|t|)\), while the separated inverse and Gram-gap bounds give an \(O(|t|)\) score displacement.  Hence the derivative of the mean bias at zero vanishes.

If only \(f\) varies coherently, then \(M_A,M_Z,\pi\), and \(B\) do not vary, so \(\delta^A_t=\delta^Z_t=0\) and (11) again gives \(E_PU(\eta_t)=\psi\).  The projector algebra gives \(B^{\mathsf T}N_t=0\); since every column of \(h_t=N_tc_t\) is also in \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\),
\[
 B^{\mathsf T}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}=0.
\]
Conditional three-view independence then gives, for every \(j\),
\[
 E_P\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\mid Y,J=j,X\}
 =\sum_{a,z}B_{(a,z),j}\{Q_tU(\eta_t)\}_{az}(Y,X)=0.
\]
Iterated expectation implies \(E_PQ_tU(\eta_t)=0\) exactly.  Thus the mean bias is identically zero along the coherent \(f\)-only path, proving the second derivative assertion.
